There once was moor covered in a deep fog impenetrable by night and only navigable by they most experienced on the brightest of days. The source of the fog remained a mystery for over one-hundred years. Even we wraiths were baffled by it. The humans that lived near it, still primitive, took to calling it, in their native tongue, the Ghosts Way. The inexperienced humans that traveled there inevitably died from exposure and starvation as they could not navigate a way out.

We wraiths decided that an investigation was in order. If something was trying to edge in on our haunting territory it had to be stopped. So I and four others set out to find the cause of the fog. We searched ceaselessly for days. Finally, though, we came upon the source of the fog. It was a peculiar type of plant. This plant released large volumes of mist from its flowers. It was decided that the flower, while not sentient in the normal way, did represent a threat. If it were allowed to spread the world itself may become covered in mist and then there would be nothing of value to haunt.

So we began the arduous task of uprooting the plants. You can imagine the difficulty as we had not brought tools for this. But we are wraiths, and we manage to do our duty. On the second day of digging it happened. The ground began to shudder, the earth began to move. The flowers rose out of the ground, and with them the beast they were attached to. It was 30 meters long, covered in a layer of mud so dense no human weapon of the period could hope to pierce it.

It should be noted that we did not fear it. We are incapable of the emotion; or it might better be said that we are the embodiment of it. We knew our duty. We had disturbed the great beast. It was our job to destroy it before it could destroy the primitive humans we so delighted in haunting. A selfish motive, but it was enough. We threw all we had at the beast and after several hours were finally able to cripple it. I gave it the final blow and the beast grew quiet. There it lay until time buried it again. The flowers have not been seen since. Though we are careful with the fog. There is always at least one wraith within the fogs that spring up from time to time.
